notice: Curated reference facts and conditional review questions, not an executable bonus or combat model. No proprietary artwork or .dat is bundled.

facts.text: Franks do not have Bloodlines in this reference tree. It is not a missing-upgrade practice target.

Frank Mill technologies are free at their respective ages in this reference. Missing Horse Collar, Heavy Plow or Crop Rotation research commands are not evidence of a mistake or proof of the final upgrade state.
The reference describes a Frank mounted-unit HP bonus starting in Feudal Age. This tool does not calculate effective HP, survivability or fight results.
facts.description_excerpt: Mounted Units +20% HP starting in Feudal Age

facts.text: The reference gives the Bohemian Spearman line +25% bonus damage. This is a capability, not an observed army or a prediction of a cavalry engagement.

Bohemian Chemistry and Hand Cannoneer availability starts in Castle Age in this reference, unlike the generic Imperial-age expectation. Neither availability nor a research/queue command confirms completed gunpowder production.
facts.description_excerpt: Chemistry and Hand Cannoneer available in Castle Age

facts.text: The reference gives Briton foot Archers +1/+2 range in Castle/Imperial Age. Actual range still depends on unit type and upgrades; it is not reconstructed from civilization alone.
facts.description_excerpt: Foot Archers +1/+2 range in Castle/Imperial Age

facts.text: The reference discounts Berber Stable units by 15/20% in Castle/Imperial Age. Queue commands cannot establish spending, completed reinforcement counts or an equal-resource comparison.
facts.description_excerpt: Stable Units cost -15/20% in Castle/Imperial Age

rules.title: Review the spear-line scouting question before further Knight commitments
rules.interpretation: Nearby spear-line and Knight queue commands make composition worth reviewing; they do not show the resulting armies or an engagement.
rules.action: If spear-line units were actually scouted, review whether available ranged support, separating the armies, or attacking elsewhere was practical before continuing the same cavalry commitment.
alternatives: Keep mobile cavalry away from spear concentrations and look for another target.
Support may already have been planned or present; these commands do not resolve the live army.
Defensive adaptation, resources, map access and information available in-game may change the choice.

rules.title: Review the Castle-age ranged-pressure scouting question
rules.interpretation: Archer-line queue commands after a recorded Castle milestone create a review question, not evidence that a ranged army was fielded or could not be reached.
rules.action: If a ranged army was scouted, compare a safe engagement or disengagement with available ranged/siege support. Check upgrades, terrain, protection and resources rather than assuming cavalry can always close the distance.
alternatives: Use mobility to avoid the concentration and threaten elsewhere if safe.
Existing support, a small enemy group or favorable terrain may make additional production unnecessary.
The replay reveals commands retrospectively; the player may not have known them in-game.

rules.title: Review reinforcement assumptions against Berber Stable commands
rules.interpretation: Stable-unit and Knight queue commands make reinforcement/composition assumptions worth checking. The reference discount does not establish either player's spending or produced army size.
rules.action: If those units were actually scouted, review reinforcement routes and composition before assuming matching queue activity means equal investment. Consider available spear-line support where appropriate, or avoid the reinforcement stream.
alternatives: Camel, Knight and light-cavalry compositions require different decisions; a generic discount does not identify the best response.
Keep mobility and choose another target if extra support is impractical.
Resources, completed upgrades, live numbers and tactical outcomes are unresolved.
